title: synced-connector-orchestrator-credential-smoothing-and-stream-ergonomics
author: Lena Chen
release_notes: Introduces a Connector Orchestrator (cross-sdk) and a Credential Concierge that smooths rotations; adds new retry profiles and a ConnectionManager used by Python/TS/Go SDKs. Small ergonomics/API surface changes to generator/async-stream helpers; bump minor versions for all SDKs.
description:
Motivation: Customers building production streaming features reported mismatched connection semantics across SDKs (token rotation + backoff + stream lifecycle), leading to occasional mid-stream auth errors and difficult-to-reproduce reconnect races. This PR introduces a lightweight Connector Orchestrator and Credential Concierge surface used consistently by Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to align behavior for retries, prefetching, and graceful stream handoffs.

What this PR does:
- Adds a ConnectionManager abstraction that centralizes: token lifecycle hooks, heartbeat/keepalive, and coordinated reconnect windows. Implementations for py/ts/go share the same retry profile definitions.
- Introduces Credential Concierge: a pluggable adapter that can drive prefetch, staggered refresh, and a small lease model (ttl-based) to avoid thundering refreshes during large-scale reconnects.
- Adds two retry templates: tidy-retry (low-latency, aggressive short backoff) and steady-retry (throughput-friendly, larger initial backoff). SDKs select sensible defaults: streaming surfaces default to steady-retry; single-request APIs keep tidy-retry.
- Harmonizes generator/async-iterator ergonomics in TS/PY so pause/resume and a "drain-and-retry" pattern are idiomatic and low-friction for users.
- Small API polish in Go to expose a typed StreamHandle and a Cancelable context for consistency with other SDKs.
- Tests, examples, and docs: new examples/connector-orchestrator (py/ts/go), unit + e2e test matrix against a local dev runtime, and console docs for the new retry presets.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (Linear ENG-827)
- [x] Proto/ABI parity verified across SDKs
- [x] Unit tests for token rotation + stream resume
- [x] Integration tests with local runtime smoke (CI matrix)
- [x] Docs and changelog entries added

Key commits (high level):
1) Add connection manager interface and TS implementation (lchen/connmgr-ts) — introduces ConnectionManager core logic and retry presets.
2) Python adapter + tests (lchen/connmgr-py) — wraps existing session manager with Concierge; adds async-generator helpers.
3) Go StreamHandle + credential concierge (lchen/connmgr-go) — typed stream handle and cancelable reconnects.
4) cross-sdk examples, docs, and version bumps (lchen/docs-bump)

Changed areas (high level):
- sdk/python/src/connection_manager.py (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/connectionManager.ts (new)
- sdk/go/stream/stream_handle.go (new)
- sdk/*/retry_profiles.ts|py|go (new/updated presets)
- examples/connector-orchestrator/ (new multi-lang examples)
- docs/reference/sdk/retries.md (new)
- ci/helm/dev-smoke.yaml (updated to include local connector)

Review summary & conversation:
- Arjun: "Nice centralization — two asks: (1) can the default steady-retry be opt-out via SDK config, and (2) add telemetry tags when a concierge issues a forced refresh so customers can alert if refresh rate spikes." Response (Lena): "Both addressed. Added `retry_profile` opt-out to SDK configs and telemetry.increment('credential.refresh.forced') in Concierge with tags (sdk_lang, env)."
- Becky: "Python async generator surface change looks good; request to keep the old iterator helper (deprecated) for one release to avoid breaking user code." Response: "Kept legacy `stream_iter()` as thin shim that logs deprecation once per process; documented migration."
- Marcus: "Go surface is pretty tight; prefer context-aware cancel semantics in StreamHandle." Response: "Implemented ctx-aware cancel and added two small e2e tests. Marcus approved on second pass."
- CI flakiness: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e in Go (network timeout). We reran the pipeline with increased timeouts for the dev runtime and added a network health check; subsequent runs passed.

Merge outcome: squash-merge on main.

Migration & compatibility notes:
- Backward compatible: most changes are additive; SDKs keep legacy constructors where possible.
- Behavior changes: default streaming retry switches to steady-retry which may increase time-to-first-success during transient auth errors but reduces overall token churn for heavy concurrent clients. Customers that relied on aggressive immediate reconnects should set `retry_profile: tidy` in config.
- Deprecations: Python `stream_iter()` is deprecated and will be removed in next minor release after one stable cycle.

Testing:
- Unit tests: 230 new/updated tests across SDKs.
- Integration: CI matrix run against dev runtime on Linux/macOS; TS/Go/py e2e smoke tests included.
- Load test: a short canary run with 200 concurrent streams to validate no token storm on solicitor cluster.

Related: linear tickets ENG-827 (design), ENG-901 (e2e gaps); support ticket SUP-1432 surfaced the original customer report.

Docs & examples:
- examples/connector-orchestrator/README.md contains guided migration steps and sample configs for Hosted vs Dedicated environments.
- Added quickstart snippets to SDK READMEs.

Version bumps:
- python-sdk v1.14.0 -> v1.15.0
- typescript-sdk v2.7.3 -> v2.8.0
- go-sdk v1.8.9 -> v1.9.0

- Announce migration note in release notes and community slack.
- Monitor credential.refresh.forced metric for one week post-deploy.
